body:
Blackstone has held the final close of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners V LP (BETP V) at its $8.7 billion hard cap. The fund is more than 50% larger than its predecessor, which closed at $5.6 billion in February 2025.

BETP V makes control investments in companies that generate and move electricity, make the equipment the grid and data centers depend on, and help energy users cut consumption. Like its predecessors, the strategy generally does not invest in owning or extracting oil and gas reserves.

“We believe there is a generational opportunity for experienced investors in the energy transition to provide solutions to the challenges posed by growing demand for electricity,” said David Foley, the global head of Blackstone Energy Transition Partners. “By backing exceptional management teams with flexible, patient equity capital to increase manufacturing capacity, recruit and train skilled labor and construct new critical energy infrastructure assets, BETP is delivering those solutions and in the process building these companies to scale, creating jobs and generating lasting value for our investors.”

Mr. Foley joined Blackstone in 1995, built the firm’s energy practice and has worked on every energy private equity investment the firm has made. He previously worked at AEA Investors and at Monitor Company. Senior managing directors on the team include JP Munfa, Bilal Khan and Darius Sepassi.

Blackstone began investing the new fund in June and has already closed on six investments. Three are platforms that build and run power generation and transmission assets, and three are acquisitions of equipment and services businesses tied to energy efficiency and grid reliability.

The platforms are Kindle Energy, an independent power producer that develops, builds and operates natural gas-fired power plants in North America; Fisterra Energy, a Madrid developer of energy transition assets that Blackstone founded in 2013 with a former Iberdrola Renovables management team led by Pedro Barriuso; and Viridon, a Chicago company that develops, builds and operates high-voltage transmission lines across five US grid regions. Kindle is building Wolf Summit Energy, a 600-megawatt gas-fired plant in West Virginia, backed by a $1.2 billion Blackstone commitment made in November 2025. Ground was broken in April 2026.

The three acquisitions came in quick succession. In July 2026, the firm agreed to buy Houston-based Dresser Utility Solutions, which makes meters, pressure regulators, relief valves and pipe repair products for gas and water utilities, from First Reserve. Later that month it agreed to buy DarkVision, a British Columbia-based company that uses ultrasound imaging and 3D software to inspect pipelines, wells and other energy infrastructure, from Koch Engineered Solutions.

In September, BETP V agreed to buy Cincinnati-based Flow Control Holdings, which makes engineered components for liquid cooling systems in data centers, a more energy-efficient alternative to air cooling, from Audax Private Equity, which is keeping a minority stake.

The new fund continues a run of activity. Since January 2025, the strategy has committed more than $11 billion of new equity, including investments in equipment makers Maclean Power Systems, Delta Star, Power Grid Components, Arlington Industries and Advanced Cooling Technologies; services businesses Alliance Technical Group and Shermco; energy data company Enverus; and gas-fired power projects Hill Top Energy Center, Wolf Summit Energy and Potomac Energy Center.

Blackstone has also been returning capital from earlier BETP funds. In July 2026, Blackstone agreed to sell Aypa Power, a North American battery storage developer with a 6.0-gigawatt portfolio, to Brookfield at an enterprise value of about $7 billion. The strategy has also sold a majority interest in Sabre Industries, which makes engineered structures for power utilities, telecom and data centers, and taken mechanical contracting and engineering firm Legence public on Nasdaq.

Blackstone says the strategy’s energy transition investments have produced a 34% net internal rate of return since 1997, as of June 30, 2026. That figure excludes investments in owning and extracting hydrocarbon reserves, which earlier funds were not barred from making. In 2025, IJ Investor named BETP its North American “Fund Manager of the Year – Equity.”

The fund series has expanded substantially since its inception. Blackstone Energy Partners closed at just over $2.5 billion in September 2012, followed by Blackstone Energy Partners II, which reached its $4.5 billion hard cap and began investing in February 2015. The third fund began its investment period in February 2020, with Blackstone reporting approximately $4.2 billion in commitments later that year. Blackstone Energy Transition Partners IV closed at its $5.6 billion hard cap in February 2025, approximately 33% larger than its predecessor, according to Blackstone.

The fundraise comes as US power demand climbs. Utilities’ five-year forecasts now call for 166 gigawatts of new peak demand between 2025 and 2030, up from 24 gigawatts in the 2022 forecasts, with data centers accounting for about 55% of the increase, according to Grid Strategies.

Utilities are spending to keep up. US investor-owned electric companies are projected to invest $220.7 billioin in 2026 and about $1.1 trillion from 2025 through 2029, roughly double their spending a decade ago, according to the Edison Electric Institute. Globally, data center power demand could rise as much as 165% by 2030 from 2023 levels, according to Goldman Sachs Research.

Other managers have raised large energy funds this year. Energy Capital Partners closed its sixth fund at $8.1 billion in August 2026, well above its initial $5 billion target and almost twice the $4.4 billion it raised for its fifth fund in May 2024.

Blackstone manages about $1.35 trillion of assets across real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Its energy transition strategy has committed more than $34 billion of equity globally.

Blackstone was founded in 1985 by Stephen Schwarzman and Peter Peterson and is headquartered in New York City.
